data.command: What is T1548.003 Bypass User Account Control?

data.text:
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ grep -A 30 "T1548.003" /opt/threat-intel/mitre-attck.yml

T1548.003: Bypass User Account Control (UAC)
  tactic: Privilege Escalation
  platform: Windows
  description: >
    User Account Control (UAC) is a Windows security feature that prompts
    users for consent or credentials when performing actions that could
    affect system security. Attackers may abuse system behaviors to bypass
    UAC, allowing them to execute arbitrary commands with high-integrity
    privileges.

  methods:
    - name: Consent Prompt Bypass
      detail: >
        Tricks the user into clicking "Yes" on a UAC consent dialog by
        masquerading as a legitimate application.

    - name: UIAccess Bypass
      detail: >
        Abuses the UIAccess flag in manifest files to grant high-integrity
        access to processes that shouldn't have it.

    - name: White-Listed Binary Abuse
      detail: >
        Leverages signed, trusted binaries (e.g., eventvwr.exe, mshta.exe,
        control.exe) that can be abused to execute code with elevated
        privileges without triggering UAC.

    - name: Registry Modification
      detail: >
        Modifies HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System
        to disable UAC (ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=0 or EnableLUA=0).

    - name: FOD Bypass
      detail: >
        Abuses Feature on Demand (FOD) installation to trigger UAC consent
        dialogs for trusted system components.

  examples:
    - eventvwr.exe /h
    - mshta vbscript:Execute("CreateObject('Shell.Application').ShellExecute('cmd.exe','','','runas',1)")
    - reg add HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

  references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/003/
    - https://www.ired.team/windows-security/user-account-control-bypass

webapp@web-srv-01:~$
